symptom: labored breathing / respiratory distress
reasoning: respiratory failure can progress to cardiac arrest within minutes; requires immediate oxygen and stabilization before any transport

symptom: open-mouth breathing
reasoning: cats are obligate nasal breathers; any open-mouth breathing indicates severe dyspnea and impending respiratory failure

symptom: cyanosis (blue, purple, or gray gums or tongue)
reasoning: cyanosis indicates severe systemic hypoxemia and tissue oxygen deprivation; cardiac or respiratory arrest is imminent

symptom: orthopneic posture: elbows flared outward, neck extended, unable to lie down
reasoning: orthopnea (inability to tolerate recumbency) indicates maximal respiratory compensation; collapse likely imminent

symptom: paradoxical chest-wall motion (chest and belly moving in opposite directions)
reasoning: paradoxical breathing pattern indicates pneumothorax or large pleural effusion severely impairing gas exchange

symptom: choking or pawing at mouth with inability to breathe
reasoning: foreign body airway obstruction; complete obstruction causes brain death within 4-6 minutes

symptom: collapse or sudden loss of consciousness
reasoning: collapse indicates cardiac arrest, severe shock, neurological catastrophe, or critical hypoglycemia; requires immediate assessment and possible CPR

symptom: pale, white, or chalky gums
reasoning: pale mucous membranes indicate shock or severe hemorrhagic anemia; perfusion is critically compromised

symptom: weak or absent pulse with rapid heart rate
reasoning: combination of tachycardia and weak pulse indicates decompensatory shock with inadequate cardiac output

symptom: cat with slow or very low heart rate and weakness (bradycardia in shock)
reasoning: unlike dogs, cats in decompensatory shock develop paradoxical bradycardia (< 150 bpm) with gray mucous membranes; this is a terminal pre-arrest finding

symptom: male cat straining in litter box with no urine output
reasoning: urethral obstruction in male cats causes fatal uremia and cardiac arrhythmia within 24-48 hours if untreated; frequently mistaken for constipation by owners

symptom: male dog straining to urinate with no output
reasoning: urethral obstruction (often from uroliths) causes progressive azotemia and cardiovascular collapse

symptom: active seizure lasting more than 5 minutes
reasoning: status epilepticus causes cerebral edema, hyperthermia, and permanent neuronal damage; requires IV benzodiazepine within minutes

symptom: 3 or more seizures within 24 hours
reasoning: cluster seizures indicate uncontrolled status epilepticus with compounding risk of cerebral edema and hyperthermia

symptom: sudden hind limb paralysis or dragging of back legs in cat
reasoning: sudden hind limb paralysis in cats is the hallmark of aortic thromboembolism (saddle thrombus); legs are typically cold and painful; time-sensitive condition with poor prognosis if untreated

symptom: sudden hind limb weakness or paralysis in dog
reasoning: acute disc herniation (IVDD) or spinal cord trauma; surgical window for decompression is 24-48 hours before permanent paralysis

symptom: head pressing against wall or furniture
reasoning: compulsive head pressing is a sign of elevated intracranial pressure, hepatic encephalopathy, or toxic encephalopathy

symptom: sudden severe ataxia / unable to stand or walk
reasoning: sudden onset inability to walk indicates central neurological event, toxin, or severe metabolic crisis requiring immediate evaluation

symptom: non-productive retching with visibly distended or bloated abdomen (dog)
reasoning: classic presentation of gastric dilatation-volvulus (GDV/bloat); stomach twists, cutting off blood supply; fatal within 1-2 hours without emergency surgery

symptom: restlessness and hypersalivation with swollen abdomen (dog)
reasoning: early GDV presentation before retching begins; large and giant breed dogs at highest risk

symptom: bright red blood or coffee-ground material in vomit
reasoning: hematemesis indicates GI hemorrhage; coffee-ground appearance indicates partially digested blood from gastric or upper GI source

symptom: large amounts of bright red blood in diarrhea with weakness or pallor
reasoning: hemorrhagic gastroenteritis or parvovirus with volume depletion and sepsis risk; small amounts of blood alone may be office_appointment

symptom: abdominal organ prolapse (tissue visible outside the body)
reasoning: evisceration requires immediate surgical correction; exposed tissue dessicates and becomes nonviable rapidly

symptom: uncontrolled bleeding soaking through bandage or cloth within minutes
reasoning: Class III/IV hemorrhage; blood volume loss >30% causes cardiovascular collapse; requires immediate compression and IV fluid resuscitation

symptom: open wound exposing bone or deep tissue
reasoning: open fractures and deep lacerations carry high infection risk and require surgical debridement within hours

symptom: penetrating chest or abdominal wound
reasoning: chest penetration causes pneumothorax; abdominal penetration risks internal hemorrhage and septic peritonitis

symptom: known ingestion of grapes or raisins (any amount, dog)
reasoning: grapes and raisins cause idiosyncratic acute renal failure in dogs; there is no established safe dose and toxicity is unpredictable; decontamination must occur before symptoms appear

symptom: known ingestion of xylitol (sugar-free gum, candy, peanut butter, baked goods)
reasoning: xylitol triggers massive insulin release causing hypoglycemia within 30-60 minutes; higher doses cause acute liver failure

symptom: known ingestion of anticoagulant rodenticide (rat poison, d-CON, warfarin bait)
reasoning: anticoagulant rodenticides cause coagulopathy with 3-7 day latency; treatment (Vitamin K) must begin before bleeding symptoms appear to prevent fatal internal hemorrhage

symptom: known ingestion of acetaminophen or Tylenol (any amount, cat)
reasoning: cats lack hepatic glucuronidation; even a single regular-strength Tylenol tablet causes methemoglobinemia and fatal hepatic necrosis within hours

symptom: known acetaminophen ingestion (large dose, dog)
reasoning: large doses in dogs cause hepatotoxicity and methemoglobinemia; less sensitive than cats but still requires decontamination and NAC treatment

symptom: heatstroke: extreme panting with disorientation or collapse after heat exposure
reasoning: core temperature >41°C causes multi-organ failure, coagulopathy, and cerebral edema; rapid cooling and IV fluids are required immediately

symptom: suspected hypothermia: cold to touch, lethargic or unresponsive, shivering stopped
reasoning: severe hypothermia (< 32°C) causes ventricular fibrillation; counterintuitively, shivering cessation means the body has lost thermoregulatory capacity

symptom: suspected hypoglycemia with seizure or collapse in diabetic pet
reasoning: hypoglycemic seizures cause irreversible neuronal death; diabetic owners should administer corn syrup to gums en route if animal can swallow

symptom: anaphylaxis after insect sting, vaccination, or medication: facial swelling with collapse or rapid deterioration
reasoning: anaphylactic shock causes distributive shock with airway compromise; epinephrine must be administered within minutes

symptom: suspected snakebite with progressive swelling, pain, or neurological signs
reasoning: pit viper envenomation causes tissue necrosis, coagulopathy, and cardiovascular collapse; antivenom window narrows quickly

symptom: active labor exceeding 1 hour of strong straining with no puppy or kitten delivered
reasoning: dystocia (obstructed delivery) risks fetal death from hypoxia and maternal uterine rupture; requires obstetric intervention

symptom: mother seizing or becoming severely weak after whelping or queening
reasoning: eclampsia (puerperal tetany) from hypocalcemia caused by lactation demands; fatal without IV calcium gluconate

symptom: eye prolapse: eyeball partially or fully out of socket
reasoning: globe proptosis requires replacement within 20-30 minutes to preserve vision; keep moist with saline-soaked cloth during transport

symptom: sudden complete blindness with dilated non-responsive pupils
reasoning: acute onset blindness in cats is often caused by hypertensive retinal detachment (secondary to CKD or hyperthyroidism); treatment within 24 hours offers best chance of vision recovery

symptom: suspected spinal trauma with inability to move one or more limbs
reasoning: spinal cord compression from fracture or dislocation; improper handling worsens injury; requires immediate immobilization and imaging

symptom: difficulty giving birth: green or black discharge before any offspring is delivered
reasoning: dark placental discharge before delivery indicates placental separation and fetal hypoxia; offspring are at risk of stillbirth

symptom: known ingestion of ethylene glycol (antifreeze)
reasoning: ethylene glycol causes rapidly progressive acute renal failure; antidote (4-MP in dogs, ethanol in cats) must be administered within 3 hours of ingestion for cats, 8-12 hours for dogs

symptom: severe burns covering a significant body area
reasoning: burns >15% body surface area cause hypovolemic shock, infection risk, and severe pain requiring immediate fluid resuscitation
